message.reasoning:
I need to choose between mortgaging a property or declaring bankruptcy.

Mortgaging St. James Place would only raise $90, leaving a $229 shortfall. I cannot cover the rent even after mortgaging everything.

I should declare bankruptcy. I considered mortgaging St. James Place first to reduce what p2 receives, but the engine says bankruptcy is appropriate when cash cannot be raised.

Mortgaging St. James Place first would give p2 $90 cash as part of the bankruptcy settlement. The property would transfer mortgaged, and p2 would have to pay 10% interest to unmortgage it.

I am weighing whether mortgaging St. James Place first is actually better for p2. If I declare bankruptcy without mortgaging, p2 would receive my $1081 cash and an unmortgaged St. James Place worth $180. However, p2 cannot immediately complete the orange monopoly because Tennessee and New York are still mortgaged.

Mortgaging St. James Place first would give p2 $1171 cash and a mortgaged property. They would have to pay $9 in immediate interest to unmortgage it. The net value is only about $1162. This is slightly better than declaring bankruptcy now, which would give p2 $1081 cash plus an unmortgaged property worth $180. But p2 could have mortgaged St. James themselves for $90, so the difference is small.

Mortgaging St. James Place first is the better strategy. It forces p2 to pay $9 in immediate interest and prevents them from instantly completing the orange monopoly by pairing it with their other mortgaged properties. I will mortgage St. James Place now, then declare bankruptcy on the next liquidation decision.
